# 🚀 Get started

📦 **Data**: [FAO Global Capture
Production](https://www.fao.org/fishery/collection/capture/en), release
**2026.1.0** (published by FAO on 2026-03-30; catches 1950–2024),
downloaded from
[Capture_2026.1.0.zip](https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip).
Licence [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
[`fao_data_info()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_data_info.md)
shows the release you use and how to cite it.

**faofishingreport** turns the FAO Global Capture Production statistics
into charts, maps and tables for reports. This page walks through a
complete first analysis of the **Eastern Central Atlantic (FAO major
fishing area 34)**; every chart below was produced by the code shown
above it.

A typical workflow:

| Step | What you do | Functions |
|----|----|----|
| 1\. Data | Check for and download the latest FAO release | [`check_fao_update()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/check_fao_update.md), [`download_fao_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/download_fao_data.md) |
| 2\. Fishing area | Total catch, main species and main countries of an area | [`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md), [`fishing_area_species()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_species.md), [`fishing_area_country()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_country.md) |
| 3\. Species and countries | Who catches a species, what a country catches | [`species_country()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/species_country.md), [`country_species()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/country_species.md), [`country_analysis()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/country_analysis.md) |
| 4\. Summaries | Composition, stock status, trends, data quality, fleets | [`stock_status()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/stock_status.md), [`peak_trend()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/peak_trend.md), [`coastal_distant()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/coastal_distant.md), … |
| 5\. Style | Language, theme, colours, map projection | [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |

## 📦 Installation

faofishingreport needs **R 4.2 or later**. Install it from GitHub:

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Linbojun99/faofishingreport")
```

All required packages (dplyr, ggplot2, sf, rnaturalearth, …) are
installed automatically.

**Windows and macOS** use binary packages, so no compiler (Rtools) is
needed. **Linux** needs the system libraries of the sf package and, for
Chinese charts, a Chinese font:

``` bash
sudo apt-get install libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev fonts-noto-cjk
```

Load the package. The start-up message shows the operating system and
the font chosen for charts (SimSun on Windows, Songti SC on macOS, Noto
Serif CJK SC on Linux):

``` r

library(faofishingreport)
#> faofishingreport: Windows, chart font "SimSun" (change it with fao_font())
```

## 💾 Get the latest FAO data

The package comes with FAO release Version: 2026.1.0, Released:
2026-03-30, Years: 1950-2024, URL:
<https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip>,
Downloaded: 2026-10-10. FAO publishes a new release about once a year.
Check whether a newer one exists and download it (about 5 MB, a few
seconds):

``` r

check_fao_update()
#> FAO Global Capture Production
#>   Latest online release: 2026.1.0 (published 2026-03-30)
#>   Bundled with package:  2026.1.0
#>   Downloaded locally:    none
#>   Your data is up to date.

download_fao_data()   # only needed when a newer release is available
```

All functions automatically use the newest data available. See [💾 FAO
data](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/articles/data.md)
for choosing releases, the data format and working with your own
subsets.

## 📁 Where the results go

Each analysis saves its charts and tables in the **current working
folder**:

| Folder | Content |
|----|----|
| `figures/png/` | Charts as PNG (always) |
| `figures/pptx/` | Charts as editable PowerPoint files (with `pptx = TRUE`; needs the eoffice package) |
| `tables/` | Tables as CSV, readable by Excel including Chinese names |

So start by choosing a folder for the report:

``` r

setwd("D:/reports/FAO34")   # any folder
```

## 🌊 First analysis: FAO area 34

[`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md)
extracts the catch of one FAO major fishing area and draws its total
catch with the breakpoints of the mean catch, its share of the world
catch, and a world map of the countries fishing there.

``` r

FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central")
```

![fishing_trend.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/fishing_trend.png`

![fishing_percentage.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/fishing_percentage.png`

![area_country_map.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area_country_map.png`

The result is a list; `FAO34$area_data` holds the catch records of the
area and is the input of most other functions:

``` r

show_table(FAO34$area_data, n = 5)
```

|  | Country..Name. | ASFIS.species..Name. | FAO.major.fishing.area..Name. | Unit..Name. | Unit | Year | Production | Production.Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|---:|:---|
| 9075 | Angola | Soles nei | Atlantic, Eastern Central | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 1970 | 0 | actual |
| 9076 | Angola | Soles nei | Atlantic, Eastern Central | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 1971 | 0 | actual |
| 9077 | Angola | Soles nei | Atlantic, Eastern Central | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 1972 | 0 | actual |
| 9078 | Angola | Soles nei | Atlantic, Eastern Central | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 1973 | 97 | actual |
| 9079 | Angola | Soles nei | Atlantic, Eastern Central | Tonnes - live weight | TLW, Number | 1974 | 0 | actual |

Any other area works the same way. The names of the FAO major fishing
areas are:

``` r

data <- load_fao_data()
sort(unique(data$FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.))
#>  [1] "Africa - Inland waters"           "America, North - Inland waters"  
#>  [3] "America, South - Inland waters"   "Arctic Sea"                      
#>  [5] "Asia - Inland waters"             "Atlantic, Antarctic"             
#>  [7] "Atlantic, Eastern Central"        "Atlantic, Northeast"             
#>  [9] "Atlantic, Northwest"              "Atlantic, Southeast"             
#> [11] "Atlantic, Southwest"              "Atlantic, Western Central"       
#> [13] "Europe - Inland waters"           "Former USSR area - Inland waters"
#> [15] "Indian Ocean, Antarctic"          "Indian Ocean, Eastern"           
#> [17] "Indian Ocean, Western"            "Mediterranean and Black Sea"     
#> [19] "Oceania - Inland waters"          "Pacific, Antarctic"              
#> [21] "Pacific, Eastern Central"         "Pacific, Northeast"              
#> [23] "Pacific, Northwest"               "Pacific, Southeast"              
#> [25] "Pacific, Southwest"               "Pacific, Western Central"
```

## 🐟 Main species and countries

The ten species with the largest catch in area 34, their catch over time
and the breakpoints of their mean catch:

``` r

species <- fishing_area_species(FAO34$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 10))
```

![area_species.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_species.png`

![area_species_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_species_wrap.png`

The same for the countries:

``` r

countries <- fishing_area_country(FAO34$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 10))
```

![area_country.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_country.png`

![area_country_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_country_wrap.png`

## 🌐 Chinese and bilingual charts

Every analysis has a `lang` argument: `"en"` (English), `"zh"` (Chinese)
or `"both"`. Country, species and area names use the official FAO
Chinese names.

``` r

species_country(FAO34$area_data, species_name = "European pilchard(=Sardine)", lang = "both")
```

![European_pilchard\_\_Sardine\_\_country_ranked_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/species/European_pilchard__Sardine__country_ranked_wrap.png`

To use Chinese everywhere, set it once with `fao_settings(lang = "zh")`.

## 📊 A first summary: stock status

[`stock_status()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/stock_status.md)
classifies each species by its catch relative to its peak catch:

``` r

status <- stock_status(FAO34$area_data)
```

![Atlantic\_\_Eastern_Central_stock_status_stocks.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/summary/Atlantic__Eastern_Central_stock_status_stocks.png`

![Atlantic\_\_Eastern_Central_stock_status_catch.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/summary/Atlantic__Eastern_Central_stock_status_catch.png`
